target_customer: US companies in agriculture, engineering, manufacturing and oil and gas that claim R&D tax credits, 179D deductions and cost segregation
problem: Corporate tax incentive studies are slow and expensive when done by CPA firms, so many eligible companies never claim them.
business_model: Tax services with AI automation, fees per study delivered by credentialed tax professionals
product_category: AI enabled tax credit and incentive services (formerly SPRX)

founders.name: Dominic Vitucci
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as the only founder; Onshore's blog signs him as CEO and CPA. Employer and school not found in sources opened.

technical_complexity.rationale: Early product automated R&D credit study preparation with AI and software integrations; the hard part is tax expertise and audit defensibility rather than novel technology.

defensibility.rationale: Traditional CPA firms and specialty credit consultancies offer the same service, and the AI workflow is copyable; credentialed staff and audit defense add some stickiness.

incumbents: Big Four and regional CPA firms
takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying or buying the company; it continued independently and raised a Series B in 2026.

market_need_then: R&D credits and similar incentives are widely underclaimed because studies are costly; the company launched its first product in December 2022 as a simple, fast and affordable R&D credit tool, per a StartupIntros listing.

branding.name_origin: Company blog (2026 rename post) says Onshore means the work stays close to the client, reasoning stays visible and a real person is accountable for every number on a return.
branding.domain_note: Now uses onshore.com; earlier brand SPRX used sprx.tax. How the .com was obtained was not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positions as accountable, evidence based tax work done with AI

rebrands.why: Announced with the Series B; the company states the name reflects keeping work close to the client with accountable people.

brand_strength.rationale: The rename came only in 2026 with the Series B; no independent brand coverage beyond funding news.

outcome_analysis: Onshore, formerly SPRX, grew to a stated 500 plus clients and over 600M USD in incentives delivered, and announced a 31M USD Series B in February 2026 with FPV leading. It combined AI with credentialed tax staff in a large underserved services market. Earlier rounds are not confirmed in primary sources.
notes: Series B confirmed by company blog and Business Wire. Vertex Holdings reports total funding of 46M USD, implying earlier rounds near 15M USD that are not itemized; ADP Ventures page labels its investment Series A but gives no amount or date, and VCBacked lists a 500K pre-seed in April 2023, both unverified. A search snippet says the CEO spent 5 years at Grant Thornton as a CPA; that page was not opened so it is not recorded. Founding year 2022 per YC, other sources say 2020. The YC page indicated the company operates as SPRX; competitor search found only 2025 to 2026 era tax AI tools (Blue J, Kintsugi), nothing dated near the 2022 launch, so the list is empty.
